extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of electric generating units (steam generating units, IGCCs, and stationary combustion turbines), compliance and environmental staff at power plants, and permitting authorities
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory compliance requirements, monitoring, calculation, recordkeeping, and reporting procedures for CO2 (GHG) emissions from affected electric generating units under 40 CFR part 60, subpart TTTT (standards of performance). Applies to stationary combustion turbines, steam generating units, and IGCCs that commence construction/modification/reconstruction in specified date ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of subpart (§60.5508)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart establishes emission standards and compliance schedules for the control of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from a steam generating unit or an integrated gasification combined cycle (IGCC) facility that commences construction after January 8, 2014, commences reconstruction after June 18, 2014, or commences modification after January 8, 2014, but on or before May 23, 2023. This subpart also establishes emission standards and compliance schedules for the control of GHG emissions from a stationary combustion turbine that commences construction after January 8, 2014, but on or before May 23, 2023, or commences reconstruction after June 18, 2014, but on or before May 23, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An affected steam generating unit, IGCC, or stationary combustion turbine shall, for the purposes of this subpart, be referred to as an affected electric generating unit (EGU).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability general requirements (§60.5509(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The GHG standards included in this subpart apply to any steam generating unit or IGCC (or stationary combustion turbine in the specified dates) that meets the relevant applicability conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicability conditions: (1) Has a base load rating greater than 260 gigajoules per hour (GJ/h) (250 MMBtu/h) of fossil fuel (either alone or in combination with any other fuel); and (2) Serves a generator or generators capable of selling greater than 25 megawatts (MW) of electricity to a utility power distribution system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — annual net-electric sales limited by permit (b)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: You are not subject to the requirements of this subpart if your EGU is a steam generating unit or IGCC whose annual net-electric sales have never exceeded one-third of its potential electric output or 219,000 MWh, whichever is greater, and is currently subject to a federally enforceable permit condition limiting annual net-electric sales to no more than one-third of its potential electric output or 219,000 MWh, whichever is greater.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — ≥50% heat input from non-fossil fuel and capacity factor limit (b)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: You are not subject if your EGU is capable of deriving 50 percent or more of the heat input from non-fossil fuel at the base load rating and is also subject to a federally enforceable permit condition limiting the annual capacity factor for all fossil fuels combined to 10 percent (0.10) or less.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — combined heat and power with permit limit (b)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: You are not subject if your EGU is a combined heat and power unit that is subject to a federally enforceable permit condition limiting annual net-electric sales to no more than either 219,000 MWh or the product of the design efficiency and the potential electric output, whichever is greater.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — effective generation capacity ≤25 MW when serving with others (b)(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: You are not subject if your EGU serves a generator along with other steam generating unit(s), IGCC, or stationary combustion turbine(s) where the effective generation capacity (determined based on a prorated output of the base load rating of each unit) is 25 MW or less.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — municipal waste combustor (b)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your EGU is not subject if it is a municipal waste combustor that is subject to subpart Eb of this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — commercial/industrial solid waste incineration (b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your EGU is not subject if it is a commercial or industrial solid waste incineration unit that is subject to subpart CCCC of this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — modification with ≤10% hourly CO2 increase (b)(7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your EGU is not subject if it undergoes a modification resulting in an hourly increase in CO2 emissions (mass per hour) of 10 percent or less (2 significant figures). Modified units not subject pursuant to this paragraph continue to be existing units under section 111 with respect to CO2 emissions standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — stationary combustion turbine unable to combust natural gas (b)(8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your EGU is not subject if it is a stationary combustion turbine that is not capable of combusting natural gas (e.g., not connected to a natural gas pipeline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — >50% heat input from industrial process without external useful output (b)(9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your EGU is not subject if it derives greater than 50 percent of the heat input from an industrial process that does not produce any electrical or mechanical output or useful thermal output that is used outside the affected EGU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — subject to subpart TTTTa (b)(10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your EGU is not subject to this subpart if it is subject to subpart TTTTa of this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: CO2 emissions standard requirement (§60.5520(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each affected EGU subject to this subpart, you must not discharge from the affected EGU any gases that contain CO2 in excess of the applicable CO2 emission standard specified in table 1 or 2 to this subpart, consistent with applicable paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance must be consistent with paragraphs (b), (c), and (d) of §60.5520, as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross vs. net energy output standard and permit requirement (§60.5520(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as specified elsewhere, you must comply with the applicable gross or net energy output standard, and your operating permit must include monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting methodologies based on the applicable gross or net energy output standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the remainder of this subpart (for sources that do not qualify under specified exceptions), where the term “gross or net energy output” is used, the term that applies to you is “gross energy output.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to use net energy output standard (§60.5520(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: As an alternate to meeting the gross-energy-output requirements, an owner or operator of a stationary combustion turbine may petition the Administrator in writing to comply with the alternate applicable net energy output standard. If granted, the affected EGU must comply with the net output-based standard and the operating permit must include monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting methodologies based on the net energy output standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners or operators complying with the net output-based standard must petition the Administrator to switch back to the gross energy output-based standard if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform fuels exception for stationary combustion turbines (§60.5520(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators of a stationary combustion turbine that maintain records of electric sales to demonstrate the turbine is subject to a heat input-based standard and are only permitted to burn one or more uniform fuels (consistent chemical composition resulting in consistent emission rate ≤69 kg/GJ) are not subject to any monitoring or reporting requirements under this subpart; they are only required to maintain purchase records for permitted fuels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform fuels include, but are not limited to: hydrogen, natural gas, methane, butane, butylene, ethane, ethylene, propane, naphtha, propylene, jet fuel kerosene, No. 1 fuel oil, No. 2 fuel oil, and biodiesel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring requirements for stationary combustion turbines burning non-uniform fuels (§60.5520(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators of stationary combustion turbines permitted to burn fuels that do not have a consistent chemical composition or that do not have an emission rate of 69 kg/GJ or less must follow the monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements necessary to complete the heat input-based calculations under this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance determination on 12-operating-month rolling average (§60.5525)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with the applicable CO2 emission standard of this subpart shall be determined on a 12-operating-month rolling average basis. For each affected EGU subject to such a standard, you must determine compliance monthly by calculating the average CO2 emissions rate at the end of the initial and each subsequent 12-operating-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See table 1 or 2 to this subpart for applicable CO2 emission standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Input-based standard calculation method (§60.5525(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If your affected stationary combustion turbine is subject to an input-based CO2 emissions standard, you must determine the total heat input from natural gas (HTIP_ng) and from all other fuels (HTIP_o) using one of the methods under §60.5535(d)(2) and use the specified equation to determine the applicable emissions standard during the compliance period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The equation uses 50 kg/GJ allowable rate for natural gas and 69 kg/GJ for other fuels (or equivalent lb/MMBtu values) in the weighted calculation of the applicable emission standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operate and maintain in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practice (§60.5525(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: At all times you must operate and maintain each affected EGU, including associated equipment and monitors, in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrator will determine if you are using consistent operation and maintenance procedures based on information that may include, but is not limited to, fuel use records, monitoring results, review of operation and maintenance procedures and records, review of reports required by this subpart, and inspection of the EGU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial compliance determination timing and first-month rules (§60.5525(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days after the end of the initial compliance period (no more than 30 days after the first 12-operating-month compliance period), you must make an initial compliance determination for your affected EGU(s). The first operating month of the initial compliance period is defined based on commercial operation dates and emissions reporting start dates, with separate rules for units commencing commercial operation on or after October 23, 2015, those prior to that date, and modified/reconstructed EGUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electric sales generated during a system emergency are excluded for applicability with the base load standard if sufficient documentation listed in §60.5560(i) is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring plan preparation and ECMPS submission (§60.5535(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: For affected sources (except certain combustion turbines), you must prepare a monitoring plan to quantify the hourly CO2 mass emission rate (tons/h) in accordance with 40 CFR 75.53(g) and (h). The electronic portion of the monitoring plan must be submitted using the ECMPS Client Tool and must be in place prior to reporting emissions data and/or monitoring system certification test results under this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The monitoring plan must be updated as necessary. Monitoring plan submittals must be made by the Designated Representative (DR), the Alternate DR, or a delegated agent of the DR (see §60.5555(d) and (e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: CO2 measurement methods — CEMS, O2 alternative, moisture monitoring (§60.5535(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: For an affected EGU that combusts coal you must, and for all other affected EGUs you may, install, certify, operate, maintain, and calibrate a CO2 continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS) to directly measure and record hourly average CO2 concentrations and a flow monitoring system. As an alternative to direct CO2 concentration measurement (provided the EGU does not use carbon separation), you may use a certified oxygen (O2) monitor to calculate hourly average CO2 concentrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If CO2 concentration is measured on a dry basis, you must also install, certify, operate, maintain, and calibrate a continuous moisture monitoring system, or use an appropriate fuel-specific default moisture value from 40 CFR 75.11(b), or petition the Administrator under 40 CFR 75.66 for a site-specific default moisture value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and quality assurance for continuous monitoring systems (§60.5535(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each continuous monitoring system used to determine CO2 mass emissions, you must meet the applicable certification and quality assurance procedures in 40 CFR 75.20 and appendices A and B to 40 CFR part 75.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not apply bias adjustment factors to exhaust gas volumetric flow rates (§60.5535(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: You must use only unadjusted exhaust gas volumetric flow rates to determine the hourly CO2 mass emissions rate from the affected EGU; you must not apply the bias adjustment factors described in Section 7.6.5 of appendix A to 40 CFR part 75 to the exhaust gas flow rate data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow monitor setup and RATA calibration requirements (§60.5535(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: You must select an appropriate reference method to set up (characterize) the flow monitor and to perform the on-going RATAs, in accordance with 40 CFR part 75. If you use a Type-S pitot tube or a pitot tube assembly for the flow RATAs, you must calibrate the pitot tube or assembly; you may not use the 0.84 default Type-S pitot tube coefficient specified in Method 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of hourly CO2 mass emissions and records (§60.5535(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate the hourly CO2 mass emissions (kg) using the specified procedures: begin with the hourly CO2 mass emission rate (tons/h) from appendix F to 40 CFR part 75 or section 4.2 of appendix F as applicable; multiply by EGU/stack operating time to convert to tons of CO2; multiply by 907.2 to convert tons to kg and round as specified. Perform this calculation only for 'valid operating hours' as defined in §60.5540(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hourly CO2 tons/h values and EGU (or stack) operating times used to calculate CO2 mass emissions are required to be recorded under 40 CFR 75.57(e) and must be reported electronically under 40 CFR 75.64(a)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Metering requirements for output-based standards (§60.5535(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If you operate a source subject to an emissions standard established on an output basis (e.g., lb CO2 per gross or net MWh), you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a sufficient number of watt meters to continuously measure and record the hourly gross or net electric output, as applicable, using 0.2 class electricity metering instrumentation and calibration procedures as specified under ANSI No. C12.20-2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a CHP EGU you must also install, calibrate, maintain, and operate meters to continuously determine and record the total useful thermal output hour-by-hour. For process steam applications, you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate meters to continuously determine and record the hourly steam flow rate, temperature, and pressure. Your plan shall ensure you install/calibrate/maintain/operate meters to record each component hour-by-hour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment of combined gross/net energy output for multiple EGUs (§60.5535(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more affected EGUs serve a common electric generator, you must apportion the combined hourly gross or net energy output to the individual affected EGUs according to the fraction of the total steam load and/or direct mechanical energy contributed by each EGU. Alternatively, if the EGUs are identical, you may apportion according to the fraction of the total heat input contributed by each EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may elect to develop, demonstrate, and provide information satisfactory to the Administrator on alternate methods to apportion the gross energy output; the Administrator may approve alternate methods if the demonstration ensures accurate estimation of emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and apportionment options for common exhaust gas stack (§60.5535(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more affected EGUs that implement continuous emission monitoring share a common exhaust gas stack, you must monitor hourly CO2 mass emissions in accordance with one of the following: (1) monitor the common stack if the EGUs are subject to the same emissions standard (sum hourly loads and use 'stack operating hours'); or (2) if EGUs have different standards, either monitor each EGU separately before mixing, or apportion CO2 mass emissions based on unit load contribution and appropriate F-factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may also elect to develop alternate apportionment methods for Administrator approval if they ensure accurate estimation of emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance demonstration — valid operating hours and exclusions (§60.5540(a)(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each 12-operating-month compliance period you must calculate the CO2 mass emissions rate using only 'valid operating hours', defined as operating hours for which: (i) 'valid data' are obtained for all parameters used to determine hourly CO2 mass emissions (and, if heat-input-based, all parameters for total heat input), and (ii) the corresponding hourly gross or net energy output value is valid data. Exclude hours where substitute data provisions of 40 CFR 75 are applied, exceedance of full-scale range of a CEMS occurs for any parameters used, or the total gross/net energy output or total heat input is unavailable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each compliance period, at least 95 percent of the operating hours must be valid operating hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of total CO2 mass emissions and determination of P_gross/net (§60.5540(a)(4)-(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each compliance period, calculate total CO2 mass emissions by summing the valid hourly CO2 mass emissions values. For each valid operating hour used, determine the corresponding hourly gross or net energy output (P_gross/net) in MWh according to the prescribed equation, including components for electric and mechanical outputs, integrated equipment, feedwater pumps, auxiliary loads, and useful thermal outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hours with no useful output: zero is considered a valid value. For hours with no gross electrical/mechanical/useful thermal output but valid CO2 mass emissions, you must still determine gross/net energy output. For hours or partial hours where gross electric output ≤ auxiliary loads, net electric output shall be counted as zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of useful thermal output (Pt_PS) for CHP and conversion factors (§60.5540(a)(5)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable (for combined heat and power), you must calculate useful thermal output (Pt_PS) using the equation: Pt_PS = (Qm * H) / CF, where Qm = measured useful thermal output flow (kg), H = enthalpy at measured temperature and pressure, and CF = conversion factor (3.6×10^9 J/MWh or 3.413×10^6 Btu/MWh).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis calculation for output-based vs heat-input-based standards (§60.5540(a)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources complying with energy output-based standards must calculate the denominator (basis) of their actual 12-operating-month emission rate by summing hourly gross or net energy outputs for all valid operating hours. Sources complying with heat input-based standards must calculate the total heat input for each fuel fired during the compliance period, including all valid operating hours and consistent with fuel-specific procedures under selected monitoring option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of CO2 mass emissions rate and rounding rules (§60.5540(a)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: If subject to an output-based standard, calculate the CO2 mass emissions rate (kg/MWh) by dividing total CO2 mass emissions by total gross or net energy output. Round off result to two significant figures if <1,000; three significant figures if >1,000. If subject to heat input-based standard, divide total CO2 mass emissions by total heat input (kg/GJ or lb/MMBtu) and round off to two significant figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting — required items including percent valid operating hours and applicable standard (§60.5555(a)(2)(iv)-(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit reports that include the percentage of valid operating hours in each 12-operating-month compliance period and, consistent with §60.5520, the CO2 emissions standard (as identified in table 1 or 2) with which the affected EGU must comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements for captured CO2 (§60.5555(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If your affected EGU captures CO2 to meet the applicable emissions standard, you must report in accordance with the requirements of 40 CFR part 98, subpart PP, and either: (1) report per part 98 subpart RR or VV if injection occurs on-site; (2) transfer the captured CO2 to an EGU or facility that reports per part 98 subpart RR or VV if injection occurs off-site; or (3) transfer to a facility that has received an innovative technology waiver from EPA pursuant to paragraph (g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver process for captured CO2 transfer requirement (§60.5555(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may request the Administrator to issue a waiver of the requirement that captured CO2 be transferred to a facility reporting under 40 CFR part 98 subpart RR or VV. To receive a waiver, the applicant must demonstrate the technology will store captured CO2 as effectively as geologic sequestration and that the proposed technology will not cause or contribute to an unreasonable risk to public health, welfare, or safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In making the determination, the Administrator shall consider operating history of the technology, whether the technology will increase emissions or other releases of any pollutant other than CO2, and permanence of the CO2 storage. The Administrator may test the system or require tests, may grant conditional approval with monitoring/reporting conditions, and may withdraw approval on evidence of releases.
